answer: Shared Operator Liability Pool: each identity's actions draw from a pool the operator funds once per identity; verified abuse triggers a payout from that pool to the victim, and the pool replenishes only at a rising rate tied to the operator's prior violations. An attacker minting many identities must keep every pool solvent, so the marginal identity costs more each round—like draining a lagoon that refills slower each time. A single bad actor leaves a comet-like trail of depleted pools behind them. Honest operators recover nectar-rate discounts after clean periods.
